findings.title: Zero Emission Credits and Renewable Energy Certificates
findings.summary: Niagara Mohawk improperly recorded monthly payments for zero emission credits (ZECs) and renewable energy certificates (RECs) that were not applicable to future accounting periods in Account 165, Prepayments. As a result, Niagara Mohawk overstated its rate base by approximately $40 million on average for each year from 2017 through 2025, resulting in overstating its Transmission Service Charge (TSC) by approximately $8 million.

recommendations.text: Revise and implement policies and procedures to ensure that REC and ZEC costs are recorded and reported in accordance with the Commission’s accounting regulations.
Provide training to relevant staff on policies and procedures implemented in response to Recommendation 1, and repeat such training as needed.

Perform an analysis to identify all REC and ZEC prepayments recorded in Account 165 and included in FERC Form No. 1 reports from 2017 through the date of the issuance of this audit report and submit the results of the analysis to DAA for review within 60 days of the issuance of this audit report.

Submit a refund analysis, within 90 days of the date of issuance of this audit report, to DAA for review that explains and details the following: (1) calculation of refunds that include the amount of REC and ZEC payments included in customer charges under Niagara Mohawk’s transmission formula rate since January 1, 2017, plus interest computed in accordance with section 35.19a of the Commission’s regulations; (2) determinative components of the refund; (3) refund method(s); (4) customers to receive refunds; and (5) period(s) refunds will be made.
File a refund report with the Commission that accords with DAA’s assessment of the refund analysis described in the previous recommendation.
Refund the amounts disclosed in the refund report to customers, with interest calculated in accordance with section 35.19a of the Commission’s regulations.

findings.title: Accounting for Operating and Maintenance Expenses (O&M)
findings.summary: Niagara Mohawk recorded various O&M expenses in a manner contrary to the Commission’s accounting regulations. This improper accounting resulted in Niagara Mohawk overstating its TSC and overbilling its wholesale transmission customers.

recommendations.text: Revise and implement policies and procedures to ensure that Niagara Mohawk properly accounts for operating and maintenance expenses consistent with the Commission’s accounting regulations.
Provide training to relevant staff on policies and procedures implemented in response to Recommendation 7, and repeat such training as needed.

Perform an analysis of A&G expense accounts for the types of costs discussed above from 2022 through the date of issuance of this audit report to identify costs that were improperly accounted for and included in Niagara Mohawk’s TSC and customer billings. Provide the results of the analysis to audit staff within 60 days of the date of issuance of this audit report.

Submit a refund analysis to DAA for review, within 90 days of the date of issuance of this audit report, that explains and details the following: (1) calculation of refunds resulting from inappropriate recoveries due to the improper accounting for the types of expenses discussed above and recorded in A&G accounts from 2022 to the present, plus interest; (2) determinative components of the refund; (3) refund method(s); (4) customers to receive refunds; and (5) the period(s) for which refunds will be made.
File a refund report with the Commission that accords with DAA’s assessment of the refund analysis described in the previous recommendation.
Refund the amounts disclosed in the refund report to transmission customers with interest calculated in accordance with section 35.19a of the Commission’s regulations.

findings.title: Accounting for Transmission Assets
findings.summary: Niagara Mohawk improperly recorded general plant assets in transmission plant accounts. As a result, Niagara Mohawk overstated its TSC, which led to overbillings to wholesale transmission customers.

recommendations.text: Revise and implement policies and procedures to ensure transmission and general plant assets are recorded in accordance with the Commission’s accounting requirements.
Provide training to relevant staff on policies and procedures implemented in response to Recommendation 19 above, and repeat such training as needed.

Perform a comprehensive analysis of plant transfers to identify all transfers that corrected one or more errors in initial functional classification for the audit period. Provide the results of the analysis to audit staff within 60 days of the date of issuance of this audit report.

Submit a refund analysis, within 90 days of the date of issuance of the audit report, to DAA that explains and details the following: (1) the calculation of refunds that resulted from correcting the misclassification of plant assets, plus interest for the audit period; (2) the determinative components of the refund; (3) the refund method; (4) customers to receive refunds; and (5) the period(s) in which refunds will be made.
File a refund report with the Commission that accords with DAA’s assessment of the refund analysis described in the previous recommendation.
Refund the amounts disclosed in the refund report to customers, with interest calculated in accordance with section 35.19a of the Commission’s regulations.

findings.title: Transmission Revenue Credits
findings.summary: In 2024, Niagara Mohawk improperly excluded certain transmission rental revenues from the revenue credit amounts used for the purposes of computing its TSC. As a result, Niagara Mohawk understated the transmission rental revenue credit, overstated its 2024 TSC revenue requirement, and overbilled wholesale transmission customers.

recommendations.text: Revise and implement procedures and policies to ensure transmission revenue credits are included in the TSC revenue requirement computation consistent with the Niagara Mohawk transmission formula rate on file with the Commission.
Provide training to relevant staff on policies and procedures implemented in response to Recommendation 25, and repeat such training as needed.

Perform an analysis of rental income accounts to identify revenues that were not properly credited to wholesale transmission customers through Niagara Mohawk’s transmission formula rates from 2022 through the date of issuance of this audit report and submit the results of the analysis to DAA within 60 days of the issuance of this audit report.

Submit a refund analysis, within 90 days of the date of issuance of this audit report, to DAA that explains and details the following: (1) calculation of refunds that include the amount of inappropriate recoveries during the audit period that resulted from the exclusion of transmission revenue credits, plus interest computed in accordance with section 35.19a of the Commission’s regulations; (2) determinative components of the refund; (3) refund method(s); (4) customers to receive refunds; and (5) period(s) refunds will be made.
File a refund report with the Commission that accords with DAA’s assessment of the refund analysis described in the previous recommendation.
Refund the amounts disclosed in the refund report to customers, with interest calculated in accordance with section 35.19a of the Commission’s regulations.

findings.title: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC)
findings.summary: Niagara Mohawk’s AFUDC rate derivation and accounting were inconsistent with the Commission’s accounting regulations. Specifically, Niagara Mohawk incorrectly (1) calculated its long-term debt cost rate; (2) included balances of Account 226, Unamortized Discount on Long-Term Debt, in the long-term debt balance for the purposes of computing long-term debt cost rate; and (3) used incorrect equity balances. As a result, Niagara Mohawk incorrectly calculated its debt and equity AFUDC rates used to accrue AFUDC.

recommendations.text: Revise policies and procedures to ensure that AFUDC is calculated consistent with Electric Plant Instruction No. 3(A)(17) and other applicable Commission requirements.
Provide training to relevant staff on policies and procedures implemented in response to Recommendation 31, and repeat such training as needed.

findings.title: Excess and Deficient Accumulated Deferred Income Tax (ADIT)
findings.summary: Niagara Mohawk improperly netted the excess and deficient ADIT related to the corporate tax rate change and associated adjustments required due to enactment of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (TCJA) and recorded the amount that resulted from this improper netting in Account 254, Other Regulatory Liabilities. This action affected the transparency and accuracy of the excess and deficient ADIT amounts reported in Niagara Mohawk’s FERC Form No. 1 filings.

recommendations.text: Revise and implement policies and procedures to ensure that Niagara Mohawk properly accounts for and reports the effect of changes in tax laws or tax rates consistent with the Commission’s accounting regulations.
Provide training to relevant staff on policies and procedures implemented in response to Recommendation 33, and repeat such training as needed.

Submit correcting journal entries to DAA, within 60 days of issuance of this audit report, with proposed accounting entries and supporting documentation that reflect corrections to recorded excess and deficient ADIT in the appropriate accounts.
